Record Class ClassName

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
be.imgn.gaia.processing.source.ClassName
Record Components:
packageName - the package, empty for the unnamed package
simpleNames - the simple names from the top-level type to this one, such as [Map, Entry]
annotations - the type annotations
All Implemented Interfaces:
TypeName, Comparable<ClassName>
public record ClassName(String packageName, List<String> simpleNames, List<Annotation> annotations) extends Record implements TypeName, Comparable<ClassName>
The name of a class, interface, enum, record or annotation type, possibly nested in others.

Names are ordered by package, then by their simple names from the top-level type, then by their type annotations as they are written, so that java.lang.String comes before java.lang.@Nullable String.

    • generatedName

      public ClassName generatedName(String kind)
      Returns the name of a top-level type generated for this one: in the same package, $, the simple names from the top-level type to this one joined by $, then $$ and the kind of the generated type. For com.example.Outer.Inner and the kind Mapper, it is com.example.$Outer$Inner$$Mapper; for the top-level com.example.Outer, it is com.example.$Outer$$Mapper.

      All the generated names of ClassName, this one, generatedName(String, String), generatedName(ExecutableElement, String) and generatedNameIn(String, String), follow one scheme, in which each type, package, method and kind gets its own name. $$ ends the names of types, packages and methods, and the kind, which has no dollar sign, comes last. A dollar sign within a name is written $0: $0 is one of the name's, $ followed by another digit numbers an overloaded method, and any other one joins two names, as no name starts with a digit. A$B.C gives $A$0B$C$$Mapper where the nested A.B.C gives $A$B$C$$Mapper. A type that is not generated can still have the name: whether a type has it already is for GeneratedSources.isAvailable(ClassName) to tell.

      Two limits come from the file systems the generated files go to, not from the scheme. Names that differ only in case, as those of methods create and Create, are distinct names but one file on a file system that ignores case, as macOS and Windows have by default; javac then reports the second file as one it already wrote. And a name is a file name: one past the 255 bytes most file systems allow, as deep packages can make with generatedNameIn(String, String), cannot be written.

      Parameters:
      kind - what the generated type is for this one, such as Mapper: a Java identifier without a dollar sign, which may be a keyword
      Returns:
      the name of the generated type, without annotations
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the kind is not an identifier without a dollar sign: if it is empty, starts with a digit, or has a dollar sign or a character that cannot be in an identifier, such as a dot or a space
      Since:
      0.1.2

    • generatedName

      public static ClassName generatedName(ExecutableElement method, String kind)
      Returns the name of a top-level type generated for a method: in the package of its type, $, the simple names from the top-level type to the method's joined by $, then $$, the name of the method, $$ and the kind of the generated type. For the method create of com.example.Outer.Inner and the kind Factory, it is com.example.$Outer$Inner$$create$$Factory. It follows the scheme of generatedName(String).

      An overloaded method, one whose type declares other methods with its name, has its number after its name: its position among them in the order they are declared, from 1, such as $Outer$$create$2$$Factory for the second create method. Declaring an overload changes the name of a method that had none. The methods the compiler declares count too, such as the valueOf(String) of an enum or the accessors of a record, in the order the type lists them.

      Parameters:
      method - the method
      kind - what the generated type is for the method, such as Factory: a Java identifier without a dollar sign, which may be a keyword
      Returns:
      the name of the generated type
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the element is not a method, such as a constructor, its type is local or anonymous, or the kind is not an identifier without a dollar sign
      Since:
      0.1.2

      Returns the name of a type generated for this one in another package, such as an implementation of an annotation type that belongs with the code using it: in that package, $$, the names of this type's package joined by $, $$, the simple names from the top-level type to this one joined by $, then $$ and the kind of the generated type. For com.example.Outer.Named, the package org.app and the kind Impl, it is org.app.$$com$example$$Outer$Named$$Impl. It follows the scheme of generatedName(String).
